newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's two biggest rail unions set Jan 30 strike.
newsitem.headline: France's two biggest rail unions set Jan 30 strike.

text.p: France's two biggest rail unions called on Wednesday for a strike on January 30 against government plans to reform the heavily-indebted SNCF state railways being debated in the Senate.

The Communist-led CGT and the Socialist-led CFDT, which between them represent a majority of the 180,000 rail workers, demanded that staff be consulted on the reform. The CGT demanded that the government drop a plan to split the SNCF with a new company taking control of the rail track.

The CFDT urged workers to hold mass meetings to set protest actions, "in the spirit of November and December 1995", when a 24-day rail strike paralysed France, forcing the government to withdraw a previous plan to streamline the railways.

Five out of eight unions are ready to back the latest SNCF reform plan which would create a state railtrack company to take over 134.2 billion francs ($24.87 billion) of SNCF debts totalling 208 billion.

SNCF chairman Louis Gallois says the overhaul, which involves a measure of regionalisation, will benefit travellers who in some cases would see cheaper fares, while rail staff will not lose their benefits.

However militant unions fear an eventual breakup of the state rail monopoly, under European Union pressure, and the loss of their civil servant status and early retirement rights, which the government failed to change in 1995.
